citation.note: appcite, cite, scholar and caselaw are 327M rows of the SAME relation under three names. This single merge is 27% of the corpus.

inferential.note: ATOMIC if-then commonsense. The single most derivability-relevant block in the corpus: these say what FOLLOWS from a situation, which is exactly the shape a dependency DAG needs. x* is the agent, o* the other party.

properties.note: This block is the one that matters for the curriculum. has-property + capable-of + used-for are what make a slot DERIVABLE from an anchor, which is the only proposal on the table for moving `acc | not copyable` off 0.003. Everything above it is bulk.

social.note: Institutional and kinship structure. Mostly from `graph` and `entity`.

bare-word.action: most are node TYPES in a relation slot -- see type_edges

lowercase-run-on.action: GitHub event types; split and map

dialects_to_reconcile.note: Seven notations for the same kind of thing, because 26 sources were built independently. The mapping is explicit and per-source; nothing is inferred by string munging at load time.

numeric-code.action: GDELT CAMEO event codes; map via CAMEO table or reject

obo-iri.action: map to canonical; keep the IRI as provenance

empty_ids.policy: REJECT and count. An id that does not parse is not a node; admitting it creates a hub that every graph statistic then reports as structure. Rejections are recorded per source in the manifest, never dropped silently.

id_space.rule: The authority segment is the naming authority, not the source that shipped the row. Two sources citing the same OpenAlex work must both produce kg:openalex:W123, or the join silently fails and the graph looks sparser than it is.

provenance.rule: Every normalised triple carries `src` (the source directory) and `orig_kind` (the pre-mapping relation string).
provenance.why: The two would-be ingestion paths do not produce facts of equal quality, and neither do 26 independently-built sources. Pooling them without recording which produced which creates a silent quality variable. `label_acc` pooled two questions in a 72:28 ratio for its entire history and the published ranking INVERTED when they were finally reported apart -- best model went from first of twelve to eleventh. No table pools sources without reporting the split.

purpose: One relation vocabulary and one id space over 26 independently-built sources, so that a fact from OpenAlex and a fact from Wikidata can be the same fact.

rejected_relations./r/RelatedTo: 989,268 rows. ConceptNet's catch-all; asserts only co-occurrence.
rejected_relations.asserted-by/claim-subject/claim-object: 475,162. Reification of the claim table itself.
rejected_relations.derived-from: 613,319. Provenance metadata, not a fact about the world.
rejected_relations.note: Deliberately NOT mapped, and counted as rejections rather than silently dropped. Each is high-volume and low-information: admitting them would add millions of edges that constrain nothing, inflate every degree statistic, and make the graph look richer than it is. This is the same judgement that kept a CSKG-only curriculum arm unregistered.

priority_order: cskg + graph -- the property and taxonomy relations, which are what derivability needs
entity (wikidata) -- the backbone that joins authorities
geo, lit, transport -- small, and carry located-in / classified-as
everything else -- bulk citation structure, normalise only if something needs it
scope.warning: 1.21 billion triples is not the deliverable. Coverage of the curriculum's vocabulary is already ~100% and WordNet's 13,810-node projection already reached it; the first KG arm returned a null with mean -0.0013 on the quarter that matters. Normalising all of scholar and caselaw would add 500M citation edges between papers the curriculum never mentions.

type_edges.action: Rewrite `<x> --org--> <y>` as `<x> --instance-of--> <y>` with the type recorded on the node, and fold into the existing 68,476 instance-of edges.
type_edges.problem: `org`, `person`, `concept`, `place`, `paper`, `airport`, `artwork`, `product`, `work` appear in the `kind` column but are not relations -- they name what the target IS. Left as relations they inflate the relation vocabulary and make `instance-of` look rarer than it is.

redundant_sources.__r2_data_catalog: the same graph as `graph/`, re-exported as Iceberg. 47 of its kinds are `graph`'s kinds. Excluded, not normalised twice.
redundant_sources.d1/*.sql: a SQL dump of the same graph, 6.5 GB. Excluded.

what_the_corpus_actually_is.unstructured_text: none. Every source is already (source_id, target_id, kind), Gutenberg and StackExchange included -- those are edge lists over catalogue entries, not prose. The planned LLM fact-mining path has nothing to mine; the whole job is normalisation.
